after.name: Question 1
after.problem: During the winter in Pasadena, the temperature, in ${F}^{∘}$, $t$ hours after $9$ a.m. can be modeled by the function $T(t)=50+14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}).$ Find the average temperature during the period from $9$ a.m. to $9$ p.m.
after.worked_solution:
Since the function is valid starting from $9$ A.M., we can conclude our interval is $[0,12].$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{12-0}{\int }_{0}^{12}(50+14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}))\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{1}{12}(50t-\frac{168}{\pi }\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}))|}_{0}^{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(50\cdot 12-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 12}{12}))-(50\cdot 0-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 0}{12}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(600-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))-(0-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(600-\frac{168}{\pi }\cdot (-1))-(-\frac{168}{\pi }\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\frac{600\pi +168}{\pi }+\frac{168}{\pi }] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(\frac{600\pi +336}{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{600\pi +336}{12\pi } \\  & ≈{58.9}^{∘}F.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The average value is (1/c)∫₀ᶜ(9+8x−3x²)dx = 9+4c−c². Setting this equal to −3 gives c²−4c−12 = (c−6)(c+2) = 0. Since c>0, c=6.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the number $c>0$ such that the average value of $f(x)=9+8x-3{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-3.$
after.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(9+8x-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}(9x+4{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}[(9c+4{c}^{2}-{c}^{3})-(0)] \\ -3 & =9+4c-{c}^{2} \\ {c}^{2}-4c-12 & =0 \\ (c+2)(c-6) & =0 \\ c & =-2,\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=6$ only.

content.problem: Find the number $c>0$ such that the average value of $f(x)=9+8x-3{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-3.$
content.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(9+8x-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}(9x+4{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}[(9c+4{c}^{2}-{c}^{3})-(0)] \\ -3 & =9+4c-{c}^{2} \\ {c}^{2}-4c-12 & =0 \\ (c+2)(c-6) & =0 \\ c & =-2,\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=6$ only.

after.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{0}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-2.
$$
